beats.vo: Two point three million blocks... one placed every three minutes, for twenty years.
How? The outside ramp theory has a problem.
To reach the top, a ramp would need to be one and a half kilometers long... bigger than the pyramid itself.
So one engineer proposed something crazy.
A spiral tunnel climbing the edges... with open corners to turn every block.
And the heaviest stones? Sixty ton granite beams.
They were lifted by a counterweight... sliding down the Grand Gallery.
A sled of stone going down... pulls the beam up.
Then, in twenty-seventeen, cosmic ray scanners found a hidden void... right above that gallery.
Thirty meters long. And nobody has entered it yet.
Should I rebuild the ancient computer next... or the Roman crane? Comment A or B.

metadata.title: The Great Pyramid Has a Ramp HIDDEN INSIDE It 🔺 #AncientTech
metadata.description:
2.3 million blocks, one every 3 minutes. An outside ramp would be 1.6 km long — so engineer Jean-Pierre Houdin proposed an internal spiral ramp and a counterweight in the Grand Gallery for the 60-ton beams. In 2017, ScanPyramids found a 30 m void above that gallery.

3D reconstruction by Ancient Tech. Comment A or B to pick the next build.

Sources: Houdin & Brier, 'The Secret of the Great Pyramid'; ScanPyramids, Nature 2017.
